sections.title: Basic Concept of Drawing Inferences
sections.content: Drawing Inferences means deriving a conclusion from the given statement that is not directly written but can be logically proven. Step 1: Read the given statement carefully. Step 2: Identify the key facts. Step 3: Choose the logical conclusion that follows from those facts. Step 4: Select the answer that can be proven 100% from the statement.

sections.title: Direct Deductions
sections.content: Direct deduction means deriving the next logical step from the information given in the statement. Step 1: Identify the explicit facts given in the statement. Step 2: Understand the relationship between those facts. Step 3: Derive a conclusion that directly follows from those facts. Step 4: Check that the conclusion does not introduce any new information. Example: Statement: All roses are flowers. Inference: Some flowers are roses.

sections.title: Avoiding Assumptions
sections.content: While making an inference, external knowledge or assumptions should not be added. Step 1: Focus only on the given statement. Step 2: Keep your general knowledge aside. Step 3: Do not select a conclusion that is only possible but not certain. Step 4: Choose only the answer that is fully supported by the statement. Example: Statement: Rahul runs every morning. Wrong inference: Rahul is healthy (this is an assumption).

sections.title: Relationship Between Statement and Inference
sections.content: An inference must always be logically connected to the statement. Step 1: Check whether the inference is a natural result of the statement. Step 2: Verify whether the inference would change if the statement changes. Step 3: If the inference introduces a new fact, it may be incorrect.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Adding personal experience or general knowledge. 2. Making assumptions using words like 'maybe' or 'possibly'. 3. Including information outside the statement in the conclusion. 4. Choosing an option that is only partially correct.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Drawing Inferences, the correct answer is the one that can be completely proven from the statement. Always rely only on the given facts and avoid adding any assumptions or external information.

tricks.title: Only Text Rule
tricks.explanation: The inference must always come only from the given statement.
tricks.example: Statement: The shop is closed today. Inference: The shop is not open today.

tricks.title: No Outside Knowledge
tricks.explanation: Do not include your general knowledge while making an inference.
tricks.example: Statement: Riya studies late at night. Wrong inference: She will top the exam.

tricks.title: 100% Certainty Test
tricks.explanation: If the conclusion is not 100% certain, it is not a correct inference.
tricks.example: Statement: All cats are animals. Inference: Some animals are cats.

tricks.title: New Information Check
tricks.explanation: If an option introduces new information, it is usually incorrect.
tricks.example: Statement: The road is wet. Wrong inference: It rained last night.

tricks.title: Keyword Focus
tricks.explanation: Pay attention to keywords such as All, Some, None.
tricks.example: Statement: All students passed. Inference: No student failed.

tricks.title: Direct Logic Shortcut
tricks.explanation: The simplest and most direct logical interpretation is often correct.
tricks.example: Statement: The meeting starts at 10 AM. Inference: Before 10 AM the meeting has not started.

tricks.title: Possibility vs Certainty
tricks.explanation: Understand the difference between a possible and a definite inference.
tricks.example: Statement: The lights are off. Possible: No one is home. Correct inference: The lights are not on.

tricks.title: Elimination Method
tricks.explanation: First eliminate options that include assumptions or extra information.
tricks.example: Statement: The library opens at 9 AM. Inference: Before 9 AM the library is closed.
